To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RV16 3c protease is sufficient in inducing chemokine expression, and does so through AP-1 and/or NF-κB.
rhinovirus 3C proteases can induce chemokine production in human bronchials cells.
the RV 3C protein is sufficient for inducing IL-8 and other proinflammatory responses, and does so by activating AP-1 and nuclear factor-κB.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which RV induces chemokine expression, which may lead to new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of RV-induced asthma exacerbations.
the mechanisms by which rhinovirus 16 induces airway epithelial cells to produce inflammatory mediators.
the mechanism by which RV16 3D protease induces IL-8 and GMSF expression in human bronchiol epithelial cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of RV16 protease is sufficient in itself to induce the expression of chemokines, which is a key factor in asthma exacerbation.
RV16 3CP is sufficient to induce IL-8 and G-CSF in human airway epithelial cells and that this occurs via an AP-1 and NFKB dependent mechanism.
RV 3 C protease induces airway cell cytokine expression in human epithelial cells, which is mediated by the AP-1 and/or NF-κB signaling pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RV16 3c protein is sufficient to upregulate the expression of IL-8 and granulocyte macrophage colony stimulating factor in 16HBE cells.
the rhinovirus protease is sufficient and necessary for inducing airway cell chemotactic responses.

the RV 3C protein is sufficient to induce IL-8 and GMSF expression in human bronchal epithelial cells, suggesting it could be a potential therapeutic target for asthma.
